label: prop:borromean-decuplet
title: The baryon decuplet as symmetric Borromean channel
html:
The baryon decuplet --- the 10-dimensional fully symmetric channel of the Schur--Weyl decomposition V^{\otimes 3} --- is realized by the Borromean baryon (Definition) with symmetric quark content.

The Schur--Weyl decomposition at N = 3, n = 3 assigns the partition \lambda = (3) to the fully symmetric subspace of V^{\otimes 3}, which has dimension \binom{N+n-1}{n} = \binom{5}{3} = 10. The 10 states correspond to the 10 elements of the weight diagram, a triangle with vertices at (3,0,0), (0,3,0), (0,0,3) in quark-count coordinates (n_u, n_d, n_s) --- that is, the corners \Delta^{++}\ (uuu), \Delta^{-}\ (ddd) and \Omega^{-}\ (sss). The remaining seven states fill the edges and the centre, with \Sigma^{*0}\ (uds) at the centre:

State Content I_3 Y
\Delta^{++} uuu +3/2 +1
\Delta^{+} uud +1/2 +1
\Delta^{0} udd -1/2 +1
\Delta^{-} ddd -3/2 +1
\Sigma^{*+} uus +1 0
\Sigma^{*0} uds 0 0
\Sigma^{*-} dds -1 0
\Xi^{*0} uss +1/2 -1
\Xi^{*-} dss -1/2 -1
\Omega^{-} sss 0 -2

Borromean realization. Each decuplet state is a Borromean baryon: three quark-unknots joined by the Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3. The symmetric partition \lambda = (3) corresponds to the Hecke symmetrizer e_{(3)} = \sum_{\sigma \in S_3} T_\sigma, which --- once normalized --- projects onto the subspace where all three strands are interchangeable. The normalization is not bookkeeping: e_{(3)} satisfies e_{(3)}^2 = c\, e_{(3)} with c = \sum_{\sigma \in S_3} q^{\ell(\sigma)}, equal to |S_3| = 6 in the classical limit, so e_{(3)} is idempotent only after division by c and the symmetric channel is identifiable with \mathrm{Sym}^3 only where c is invertible. In characteristic 2 or 3 it is not, and the identification fails.

What the Borromean topology does and does not supply. The Borromean link carries an S_3 symmetry permuting its three components, so it is a consistent carrier for the symmetric channel. It does not, however, select that channel: the octet (2,1) and the singlet (1^3) live on the same three strands and are equally available to the same link. Brunnian-ness --- that removing any one component frees the other two --- is a statement about sublink triviality, and no argument in this framework connects it to the Young-symmetriser decomposition of V^{\otimes 3}. The channel selection is carried entirely by the Hecke projector, not by the topology.

Missing ingredient: spin and colour. The physical decuplet is spin-3/2, and what forces the flavour-symmetric channel for it is the requirement that the total wavefunction be antisymmetric once three-colour degrees of freedom are included, as originally proposed via parastatistics by O. W. Greenberg [greenberg1964] and via explicit three-triplet \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} symmetry by M. Y. Han and Y. Nambu [han-nambu1965]: with colour antisymmetric and spin symmetric, flavour must be symmetric. This chapter derives neither the spin factor nor the colour antisymmetry, so the identification \lambda = (3) \leftrightarrow decuplet is at present a matching of dimensions and weights, not a derivation of the spin--flavour--colour selection rule. This is recorded as an open item in the open-problems section.

Octet versus decuplet and quantum dimension balance. The mixed partition \lambda = (2,1) gives the 8-dimensional baryon octet (proton, neutron, \Sigma, \Lambda, \Xi). The antisymmetric partition \lambda = (1^3) gives the singlet. The distinction between octet and decuplet is entirely carried by the Hecke module: the S^{(3)} projector (one-dimensional) selects the decuplet, while the S^{(2,1)} projector (two-dimensional) selects the octet. Over any field and for every q \neq 0, the quantum dimensions \dim_q(\mathbf{10}) = (q^2 + q^{-2})[5]_q, \dim_q(\mathbf{8}) = [2]_q[4]_q, and \dim_q(\mathbf{1}) = 1 satisfy the identity

  (q^2 + q^{-2})[5]_q + 2\,[2]_q[4]_q + 1 \;=\; [3]_q^3,

normalizing the rank-3 Ocneanu weights w_\lambda(q, z_3) = \dim_q(V_\lambda)/[3]_q^3 at z_3 = q^3/[3]_q to w_{(3)} + 2\,w_{(2,1)} + w_{(1^3)} = 1 ($10.6690 + 2 \times 8.2641

  • 1 = 28.1973 = [3]_{q_0}^3atq_0$).

Conditional on N = 3. As with all eightfold-way content, this derivation is conditional on the flavor fundamental being three-dimensional (Proposition). Realised on degree-3 homogeneous polynomials, \dim_K \mathrm{Sym}^3(W_3^*) = \binom{5}{3} = 10 whereas \dim_K \mathrm{Sym}^3(V_2^*) = \binom{4}{3} = 4, so at N = 2 the symmetric partition (3) yields only a 4-dimensional spin-3/2 quadruplet, not a decuplet.
